en: The Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Great Eloquence,
Great Universal Wisdom, and Special Advancement to the Trial Position of Court Ceremonial Official, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata,
having attained perfect enlightenment at the summit of the fourth dhyāna in the Peak of the Form Realm,
immediately descended from the peak of Mount Sumeru.
Within the Vajra-jewel pavilion,
all Tathāgatas throughout the entirety of space and the whole of the Dharma-realm gathered like clouds;
surrounding him from front and back, they spoke with one voice in unison:
I only pray that the World-Honored One will turn the wondrous Dharma wheel of profound secrecy—
namely, the Vajradhātu wheel and the Trailokyavijaya command wheel.
The wheel of universal subjugation and the wheel of the accomplishment of all aims—
these four wheels emerge from the heart of Vairocana.
Each wheel contains thirty-seven noble ones;
for each mantra, there is a corresponding samādhi,
mudrā, ritual gesture, and prescribed conduct.
By the power of the vow of great compassion,
[he manifests] in defiled buddha-fields and in pure, wondrous worlds.
Sometimes hidden and sometimes manifest,
the Tathāgata Vairocana turns the wheel [of Dharma] to bring benefit and happiness, delivering all sentient beings in ways that differ for each individual.
Having received the requests of all the Tathāgatas and wishing to turn the wheel of Dharma,
he immediately entered samādhi.
He beheld Maheśvara, the Great Lord, who was stubborn,
difficult to transform, and clung to false views;
he perceived that his own body of tranquil great compassion was not capable of taming such a being.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi of Compassionate Wrath.
From the center of his chest, he manifested the Great Bodhicitta as a five-peaked vajra,
from which emerged the body of the Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya— possessing four faces and eight arms, blazing with majestic power, and wondrously difficult to behold.
He prostrated himself before Vairocana Tathāgata and all the Buddhas,
saying: "I pray only that the World-Honored One will instruct me as to what I should do."
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya:
"You shall now subdue those great devas who are difficult to tame,
causing them all to take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and to resolve upon bodhicitta."
Immediately, all the devas were subdued and they all took refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
with the sole exception of Maheśvara.
Possessing immense majesty, he arose to resist his enemies.
The Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya subdued him with various forms of suffering even unto death; he trampled Mahādeva under his left foot and Mahādevī under his right. Thereupon, Vairocana Tathāgata...
Having entered the samādhi of great compassion and pity,
he then spoke the Vajra Life Span Dhāraṇī and further entered the Vajra Life Span Samaya.
Furthermore, by binding the secret mudrā and empowering Mahesvara Deva-rāja,
he was restored to life and his lifespan was further increased;
he took refuge in all Buddhas and resolved to attain bodhicitta.
Through the empowerment and prophecy, one attains the eighth stage.
This is the Vajrāyus-mantra: Oṃ vajrayuṣe sarvaha. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajradhara:
If there are good sons or good daughters who receive,
uphold, and recite [this mantra] three times each day, one thousand times per session,
all their past and present evil karmic causes and conditions leading to short life and premature death shall be extinguished.
By upholding this mantra, one's faith becomes pure,
karmic obstructions are eliminated, and one's lifespan is further increased.
This applies to those who practice samādhi as well.
In this very life, one shall not be subject to the cycle of rebirth through the physical body born of parents,
but shall attain the five supernormal powers and move freely through the air.
Next, one should recite the Armor-Mantra for Protecting the Body, which says:
Oṃ vajra-jvala. Next, one should visualize the syllable *ja* (jra), its radiance shimmering and illuminating everywhere.
One becomes the Bodhisattva Mahāvajrāyus.
Next, one invites the Bodhisattva by means of the four-syllable vidyā-mantra to descend into the maṇḍala and receive all offerings.
The four-syllable mantra is:
JAH HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ. At that time, the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
The *Vajrāyur-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, [copied] in the fifth month of the fourth year of the Enpō era.
Copied from the Katsurao Collection manuscript.
The Vinaya Master Jōgen copied it from the Uji Keishin-in manuscript in the *kōshitsu* year of the first year of Tenmei (1781).
Jinin obtained this manuscript this year and had it transcribed.
It was collated using printed woodblocks.
This sutra is, in fact, an abbreviated version of the preceding sutra.
For those unable [to read the full text], only the "Essence of the Eye" (Kankyō) is shown;
this is not a separate edition.
Completed with added annotations on the sixth day of the fourth month of the Guihai year. Jishun.
